literal: Whatever good deed / to those who destroyed even / escape / there is / escape / is not / done good deed / who destroyed / to the person
translation: There is redemption for those who have destroyed any other virtue, but there is no redemption for one who destroys the memory of a good deed done to them.
modern: எந்த அறத்தை அழித்தவர்க்கும் தப்பிப் பிழைக்க ஒரு வழி இருக்கும். ஆனால், ஒருவர் செய்த உதவியை மறந்து அழித்தவனுக்குத் தப்பிப் பிழைக்க வழியே இல்லை.
explanation: The couplet contrasts the destruction of general virtues with the destruction of gratitude. The word 'கொன்ற' (killed/destroyed) is used metaphorically to mean ruining or completely forgetting a virtue or a good deed. While a person might find a way to redeem themselves after committing other wrongs, the text asserts that there is absolutely no salvation for someone who is ungrateful for the help they have received.
